method.scope: Seed corpus for coupling reverse physics, reverse mathematics, weak-choice analysis, constructive mathematics, topos quantum theory, operational reconstruction, and Krein geometry.
method.selection: Primary research and an authoritative reverse-mathematics monograph were preferred. Local entries are pinned reports that define this repository's existing separation discipline.
method.pinning: Remote PDF bytes were fetched on 2026-08-11 and SHA-256 hashed without vendoring. Local reports are pinned by Git blob and repository commit. One historical metadata record is explicitly unpinned.
method.verification_boundary: Hashes establish identity of consulted bytes, not correctness of the papers. The ledger is a literature receipt and does not independently reproduce any cited theorem.

entries.citation: Gabriele Carcassi and Christine A. Aidala, Reverse Physics: From Laws to Physical Assumptions, Foundations of Physics 52, 40 (2022).
supported_statements: Reverse physics asks which physical assumptions are sufficient or necessary for physical laws, by analogy with reverse mathematics.
entries.boundary: Defines the reverse-physics programme; it does not classify the logical or set-theoretic strength of the mathematics used by a physical theory.

entries.citation: Stephen G. Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, second edition, Cambridge University Press (2009).
supported_statements: Reverse mathematics classifies the set-existence axioms needed for theorems of ordinary mathematics over explicit weak base theories.
Complete separable metric spaces belong to the intended scope of ordinary countable mathematics even though their point sets may be uncountable.
entries.boundary: The standard second-order-arithmetic programme is not by itself a formalization of a physical theory or of arbitrary set-sized functional analysis.

entries.citation: Benedict Eastaugh, Computational reverse mathematics and foundational analysis (2018).
supported_statements: Foundational analysis uses reverse mathematics to compare what different foundational programmes can justify.
The choice of entailment and model class can itself exceed the resources of the foundation being assessed.
entries.boundary: A methodological analysis, not a physics application or a theorem that one reverse-mathematical framework fits every target.

entries.citation: Robert M. Solovay, A model of set-theory in which every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable, Annals of Mathematics 92 (1970), 1-56.
supported_statements: Relative to an inaccessible-cardinal assumption, there is a model of ZF with dependent choice in which every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable.
entries.boundary: Dropping Choice alone does not imply that every set of reals is measurable; this is a relative-consistency construction with additional strength in the metatheory.

entries.citation: Stefano Rossi, The Banach-Alaoglu theorem is equivalent to the Tychonoff theorem for compact Hausdorff spaces (2009).
supported_statements: Over ZF, the full Banach-Alaoglu compactness statement and Tychonoff compactness for compact Hausdorff spaces have the Boolean-prime-ideal or ultrafilter strength described in the paper, strictly below full Choice.
entries.boundary: A theorem about general compactness principles; it does not show that every concrete PDE or quantum construction uses that full generality.

entries.citation: Bruce Blackadar, Ilijas Farah, and Asaf Karagila, Hilbert Spaces Without The Countable Axiom of Choice, revised 2026.
supported_statements: Hilbert spaces and their operator theory can be studied in ZF without countable Choice, and pathologies expose distinctions hidden by ZFC.
The assertion that every Hilbert space has the familiar basis behaviour is not a definition-level truth independent of set theory.
entries.boundary: Foundational Hilbert-space analysis, not evidence that a particular physical Hilbert space exhibits the pathological examples.

entries.citation: Bruce Blackadar and Ilijas Farah, Separable C*-algebras Without the Countable Axiom of Choice (2026).
supported_statements: A substantial theory of separable C*-algebras, including representation, polynomial spectral mapping, and continuous functional calculus for commuting normal elements, can be developed in ZF.
Without Choice, nonseparable examples can break familiar state-space and commutative representation conclusions.
entries.boundary: Does not automatically remove Choice from AQFT, interacting QFT, state selection, or nonseparable operator-algebra arguments.

entries.citation: Thierry Coquand and Bas Spitters, Constructive Gelfand duality for C*-algebras, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 147 (2009), 339-344.
supported_statements: Commutative Gelfand duality admits a constructive formulation in which spectra are handled point-free.
entries.boundary: Constructive commutative duality is not a complete constructive formulation of interacting quantum field theory.

entries.citation: Chris Heunen, Nicolaas P. Landsman, and Bas Spitters, A topos for algebraic quantum theory, Communications in Mathematical Physics 291 (2009), 63-110.
supported_statements: An algebraic quantum system can be represented internally in a topos with an intuitionistic Heyting logic and a localic spectrum.
entries.boundary: A reformulation of algebraic quantum theory; it does not establish empirical superiority, eliminate all external classical reasoning, or construct Weyl QFT.

entries.citation: Lucien Hardy, Quantum Theory From Five Reasonable Axioms (2001).
supported_statements: Finite-dimensional quantum formalism can be reconstructed from operational axioms, with continuity doing explicit work in separating the quantum and classical cases in this framework.
entries.boundary: Finite-dimensional reconstruction under its stated framework; it does not establish the foundations of infinite-dimensional QFT or the set-theoretic strength of the reconstruction proof.

entries.citation: Giulio Chiribella, Giacomo Mauro D'Ariano, and Paolo Perinotti, Informational derivation of quantum theory, Physical Review A 84, 012311 (2011).
supported_statements: Within an operational-probabilistic framework, five informational axioms define a broad class and purification selects quantum theory without taking Hilbert space as the starting postulate.
entries.boundary: A reconstruction result in its declared operational framework; its proof has not yet been audited for logical or choice strength here.

entries.citation: K. Esmeral, O. Ferrer, and E. Wagner, Frames in Krein spaces arising from a non-regular W-metric, Banach Journal of Mathematical Analysis 9 (2015), 1-16.
supported_statements: A Krein space has an indefinite product together with a fundamental symmetry whose associated positive product supplies a Hilbert-space topology.
entries.boundary: A mathematical structural fact; it neither validates a generalized Born rule nor removes set-theoretic assumptions from infinite-dimensional analysis.

entries.citation: Sam Bateman and Neil Turok, Escape from Ostrogradsky via Hidden Ghost Parity (2026).
supported_statements: The Bateman-Turok proposal changes the state-space metric and adjoint/probability structure by using a Krein carrier and a fundamental ghost parity.
entries.boundary: The paper's tree-level positivity and deferred operator claims retain the boundaries audited in the repository; no foundational-strength result follows from this citation.

entries.citation: weyl-gravity repository, Physics, geometry, mathematics -- the separation ledger.
supported_statements: This repository already separates physical postulates, imported geometry, and proved mathematics, and requires independence witnesses and level-specific claims.
entries.boundary: The report explicitly does not yet separate object mathematics from foundational and metalogical assumptions.

entries.citation: weyl-gravity repository, The weakenable base -- recognised, not invented.
supported_statements: Carrier construction constraints can be made into a weakenable base, but the repository's existing lattice is structural rather than a logical reverse-mathematics theorem.
entries.boundary: No proof system or logical independence result is supplied by the carrier lattice alone.

unresolved: The Carcassi-Aidala paper is currently metadata-pinned only; acquire and hash an authoritative full-text artifact before a source-freeze.
No source in this seed corpus proves that an empirically stated physical postulate implies full Choice over a weak base.
The logical and choice strength of the Hardy and Chiribella-D'Ariano-Perinotti reconstruction proofs has not been classified.
The choice strength of the specific spectral, Green-operator, state-selection, and renormalization theorems used in this repository remains unaudited.
Finite, constructive, predicative, ZF, ZF+DC, and topos-internal formulations are not interchangeable and require separate formal targets.
